summary: Wrote a 13-phase implementation plan for consent-gated git push: a single-use, HMAC-signed, target-bound grant minted only by a literal human prompt (UserPromptSubmit), enforced by a new push guard hook plus a sanctioned wrapper, with registration in both settings templates, five test suites, the /please command and rule narrowing, and the orchestrator relay leg. Three planning-time decisions extend the research: consumption is shared between hook and wrapper (because /merge, /tag and cslib /pr all push inline), the mint hook recognises /merge, /tag and /pr so those user-only flows keep working with zero cslib edits, and the default-branch exclusion is narrowed to force forms only (surfaced as a non-blocking user_decision).

artifacts.summary: 13-phase, 17.5-hour plan across 8 dependency waves covering grant semantics, the enforcement pair, the /please command, the docs sweep, and the dispatch relay.

user_decision.question: Consent-gated push: may a plain (non-force) push of the default branch be authorized by a /please grant, or should every push to the default branch stay categorically excluded as the research report recommended?
options: Admit plain non-force default-branch pushes under a valid grant; keep every force form on the default branch, bare --force anywhere, and all bulk/deletion refspecs categorically excluded (planner's recommendation - git-workflow.md's pre-existing Never Run is specifically force-to-master, and this repo's own working branch IS master, so a blanket exclusion would make the mechanism unusable here)
Exclude every push to the default branch from any grant, per the research report's stricter recommendation; a push from this repository would then always require a non-default branch
user_decision.recommended: Admit plain non-force default-branch pushes under a valid grant; keep every force form on the default branch, bare --force anywhere, and all bulk/deletion refspecs categorically excluded (planner's recommendation - git-workflow.md's pre-existing Never Run is specifically force-to-master, and this repo's own working branch IS master, so a blanket exclusion would make the mechanism unusable here)
